claims.assertion: The periodic group had lower measured leg-press 1RM after cessation than immediately before cessation.
claims.limitations: Within-arm contrast, no interruption-specific randomized counterfactual for this estimate; untrained population and one movement.
claims.assessment: Supervised prior training and explicit repeated tests; attrition and transfer limit applicability.

support.locator: Results §3.3, Fig. 4; Table 3 leg press row
support.result: Mean individual percent change −5.4% ± 4.4% SD; p<.001.
support.restriction: SD describes dispersion, not CI; no individual decay rate or approved transfer.

claims.assertion: The study did not detect a difference in leg-press strength gains between periodic and continuous schedules across their active training periods.
claims.limitations: No equivalence test; differently timed schedules; untrained sample and completer attrition.
claims.assessment: Randomized comparison with supervised training; direct between-group CI not extracted.

support.locator: Results §3.2.2, Table 3 leg press row; Fig. 4
support.result: Periodic +43.8 kg (95% CI 33.8–53.7); continuous +41.9 kg (36.4–47.4); no detected group-by-time difference.
support.restriction: Within-arm CIs; cannot infer equal results for uninterrupted training of the same total calendar duration or experienced hybrid athletes.

claims.assertion: The planning-prompt group did not demonstrate higher gym attendance than the recall-prompt group in the respondent sample.
claims.limitations: Short horizon, survey participation may select respondents, attendance does not establish training fidelity or outcomes.
claims.assessment: Randomized prompt with electronically recorded visits; no transfer approved.

support.result: Planning minus recall −0.30 visits (95% CI −0.71 to 0.11), n=877 respondents.
support.restriction: Specific prompt and population; not a comparison of adaptive training plans.

claims.assertion: Flexible attendance incentives produced more weekly gym visits during the intervention than restricted-window incentives in the pooled comparison.
claims.limitations: Workplace setting, financial rewards, short horizon, gym attendance rather than adherence or performance.
claims.assessment: Randomized incentive conditions with objective attendance; clustered SE; post-intervention evidence less precise.

support.locator: Table 2 Panel A, column 7, Flexible minus Routine Wald test
support.restriction: During incentive intervention only; no approved transfer to ordinary hybrid coaching or durable habit.

methods.question: longitudinal-coaching-continuity
methods.description: Preserve athlete-confirmed objectives and an approved current block while recording conditional successor intentions; revisit at meaningful review or event changes.
methods.provenance: Packet 010 sections 3–4, LT-P01/02/05/07; extends Packet 006 hierarchical block methodology and Packet 009 contextual history review.
methods.tradeoffs: No optimal horizon or transition cadence established; explicit approval for active objective or block changes; event conflicts may require revised priorities.

methods.question: longitudinal-coaching-continuity
methods.description: Distinguish known missed work, retained exposure and uncertain capacity; protect remaining priority sessions, select credible introductory exposures when necessary, and do not automatically repay missed work.
methods.provenance: Packet 010 LT-P03/04, section 4.3; extends IA-P03/05, HP-P02/09 and recovery-aware review.
methods.tradeoffs: No universal restart fraction; clinical restrictions override historic success; old PRs do not establish current tolerance.

methods.question: longitudinal-coaching-continuity
methods.description: Review confirmed deviations and observation coverage; ask about time, preferences and burden, then offer compatible feasible alternatives or seek explicit objective revision.
methods.provenance: Packet 010 LT-P06/07 and section 4; original practical methodology.
methods.tradeoffs: Attendance research is indirect and incentive-specific; avoid motivation labels; changes remain subject to restrictions, secondary commitments and approval.
